summary: Receives full DAT tables over the network from a Touch Out DAT, making it useful for synchronizing tabular state between TouchDesigner processes rather than processing individual messages.

key_params.name: protocol
key_params.note: Streaming TCP/IP, UDP messaging, or multicast UDP transport

key_params.name: address
key_params.note: Multicast listen address or UDT server address depending on protocol

key_params.name: port
key_params.note: Network port that receives Touch Out packets

key_params.name: shared
key_params.note: Share a connection with other networking DATs using the same protocol

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Enable receiving; when off, incoming data is not retained

key_params.name: messages_pending
key_params.note: Pending network message count for diagnostics

key_params.name: customext
key_params.note: Custom editor extension when extension mode uses a custom extension

common_gotchas: Touch In DAT expects a Touch Out DAT peer and receives whole table states, not arbitrary message rows.
Port, protocol, address, and multicast settings must match the sender before any table updates appear.
Turning Active off drops network data received during that period.
Large or frequently changing tables can be more expensive than message-based UDP/TCP DAT workflows.
Use UDP In DAT or TCP/IP DAT when the design needs packet/message callbacks instead of table synchronization.
key_concepts: Touch In DAT receives whole DAT tables from Touch Out DAT instead of packet-style message rows.
Protocol, address, port, and shared connection settings must match the sender for table synchronization.
The Active parameter controls whether incoming table updates are accepted or dropped.
It is a higher-level table sync tool; UDP/TCP DATs are better for arbitrary messages and callbacks.
